(p-247) Surah al-Jumu'ah (The Congregation)

Medinan, and its verses are eleven.

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies Allah﴾, glorifying Him continuously.

﴿The Sovereign, the Holy One, the Mighty, the Wise﴾. The four attributes have also been recited in the nominative case, by way of praise (madh).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 62, verse 2:

﴿He it is who raised among the unlettered (ummiyyin) a Messenger from among themselves﴾. That is: among the Arabs, because most of them did not write or read. It is said: writing first appeared in al-Ta'if, which took it from the people of al-Hira, and they were from the people of al-Anbar.

﴿A Messenger from among themselves﴾. That is: one who is of their number, unlettered like them.

﴿Reciting to them His verses﴾. Despite his being unlettered like them, it was not known of him that he recited or learned.

﴿And purifying them﴾. This is another attribute of "a Messenger," conjoined to "reciting" (yatlu). That is: he leads them to what makes them pure from the vile beliefs and deeds.

﴿And teaching them the Book and the Wisdom﴾. This is another attribute of "a Messenger," arranged in existence after the recitation. But he placed purification between the two, which is an expression for perfecting the soul according to its practical faculty and refining it, and for perfecting it according to the theoretical faculty, which is attained through teaching that follows the recitation. This is to signal that each of these arranged matters is a magnificent blessing in its own right, deserving of gratitude. Had the order of existence been observed, it would have come to mind that the whole is one single blessing, as was mentioned in Surat al-Baqara. This is the secret in referring to the Qur'an sometimes as "verses" and sometimes as "the Book and the Wisdom," as a symbol that, considering each title, it is a blessing on its own. The inclusion of the Wisdom of what is within the prophetic hadiths of rulings and laws does not detract from this.

﴿And indeed they were before in manifest error﴾. Of polytheism and the corruption of the Age of Ignorance. This is an explanation of the intensity of their need for someone to guide them, and a removal of what might be imagined of his, peace and blessings be upon him, having learned from others. "In" here is the light (mukhaffafa) form, and the "lam" is the differentiating lam (lam al-fariqa).

Qur'anic quotations go in ﴿ ﴾ with plain translations inside. Technical terms are transliterated with glosses on first occurrence.

﴿And others among them﴾ is conjoined either to "the unlettered ones" (al-ummiyyin), or to the object-pronoun in "He teaches them" and "teaches others among them." That is: from among the unlettered, namely those who came after the Companions until the Day of Religion (yawm al-din). His call (da'wah) and his teaching, peace and blessings be upon him, encompass all of them.

﴿who have not yet joined them﴾ is a descriptive clause (sifah) qualifying "others." That is: they have not yet joined them, but they will join them.

﴿And He is the Almighty (al-'Aziz), the All-Wise (al-Hakim)﴾: the one who is absolute in might (al-'izzah) and wisdom (al-hikmah). For this reason He empowered an unlettered man (ﷺ) with that great matter (p-248) and chose him from among all of mankind.

﴿That﴾: the distinction by which he stands out from among the rest of mankind.

﴿The bounty of Allah﴾: His favour and His beneficence.

﴿He bestows it upon whom He wills﴾: as a preference and a gift.

﴿And Allah is the Lord of the Mighty Bounty﴾: the bounty before which the delights of this world and the delights of the Hereafter are regarded as insignificant.

﴿The likeness of those who were burdened with the Torah﴾ means: those who were taught it and charged with acting upon it.

﴿then did not bear it﴾ means: they did not act upon what is in its contents of verses, among which are the verses that clearly testify to the prophethood of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

﴿is like the likeness of a donkey carrying books﴾ means: books of knowledge, which tire it to carry and from which it gains no benefit. The word "يَحْمِلُ" (yahmilu, "carrying") is either a *ḥāl* (circumstantial clause, describing the state of the subject), in which case its governing element is the sense of "likeness" (*mathal*), or it is an attributive clause (*ṣifa*) modifying "الحِمارِ" (al-himār, "the donkey"). The donkey here is not a specific one, so it has the status of an indefinite noun, as in the line of one who said: "And I pass by the miser who insults me."

﴿Evil is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of God﴾ means: evil is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of God. This is on the basis that the *tamyīz* (specifying noun) is omitted and the agent (*fā'il*) it explains is hidden within the verb, and "مَثَلُ القَوْمِ" (mathalu al-qawm, "the likeness of the people") is the *makhṣūs bi-l-dhamm* (the one singled out for censure). The relative clause is then an attribute of "the people." Alternatively, the meaning is: evil is the likeness of the likeness of those who denied... etc., on the basis that "مَثَلُ القَوْمِ" is the *fā'il* of "بِئْسَ" (bi'sa, "evil is"), and the *makhṣūs bi-l-dhamm* is omitted; it is the Jews who denied what is in the Torah of the verses that bear witness to the authenticity of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿And God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ means: those who place denial in the place of affirmation, or who wrong themselves by exposing themselves to everlasting punishment.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 62, verse 6:

﴿Say, O you who are Jews﴾ i.e., those who have become Jews (tahawwadu).

﴿If you claim that you are the allies of God to the exclusion of other people﴾ They used to say: "We are the sons of God and His beloved," and they claimed that the Abode of the Hereafter is exclusively theirs with God, and they would say: "None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews (hud)." So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was commanded to say to them, to make manifest their lie: "If you claim that."

﴿then wish for death﴾ i.e., then wish from God that He cause you to die and transfer you from the abode of tribulation to the abode of honor.

﴿if you are truthful﴾ Its answer is omitted, because of what precedes it indicating it: "if you are truthful in your claim and certain that it is true, then wish for death, for whoever is certain that he is among the people of Paradise loves to be delivered to it from this abode, which is the dwelling place of troubles."

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 62, verse 7:

﴿And they will never wish for it, ever.﴾ This is a report of what will come to pass from them. The particle "bi" in His saying, ﴿because of what their hands have sent forward﴾, is connected to what the negation implies, i.e., they refuse to wish for it (tamanni) because of what they did of disbelief and sins that necessitate entry into the Fire. And since the hand (yad) is, among the limbs of a human being, the locus of most of his actions, it is used figuratively at times for the self (nafs) and at other times for power (qudrah).

﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾ That is, Knowing of them. The choice of the explicit noun "the wrongdoers" over a pronoun is to condemn them and to record upon them that they are wrongdoers in everything they do and everything they leave undone, among which is their claim to what they are far removed from. The sentence is a concluding clause (tadhyil) to what precedes it, confirming its content: He is Knowing of them and of the various kinds of wrongdoing and sins that proceed from them, which lead to the varieties of punishment, and of what will come from them of avoiding what leads to that. So the matter occurred as He mentioned, and none of them wished for death, as His saying, the Exalted, indicates:

Say: ﴿Indeed, the death from which you flee﴾. This is said to them only after their flight from wishing for it has become evident. The Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, said: "If they had wished for death, they would have died on the spot." This is one of the miracles (al-mu'jizat). That is: the death from which you flee, and do not dare to wish for, for fear of being seized by the consequence of your disbelief.

﴿Then indeed it will meet you﴾ definitely, with no diverting force to turn it aside and no averting protector to hold it back. The particle al-fa' (the fa' particle) is used to make the noun (al-ism) carry the meaning of a conditional (al-shart) by way of the descriptive quality. It has also been read (qira'a) without it, and it has been read as "the death from which you flee, it will meet you."

﴿Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ Who nothing hidden escapes.

﴿So He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ of disbelief and sins, by requiting you for them.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 62, verse 9:

﴿O you who have believed, when the call is proclaimed for the prayer⁠—﴾ That is: when the call (nida') is made for it, i.e., when the adhan is called for it.

﴿from the day of Friday⁠﴾ This is an explanation of "idha" (when) and a clarification of it. It was also said that "min" (from) here carries the meaning of "fi" (in), as in His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Show me what they have created from the earth﴾ [35:40], i.e., in the earth. It is called "Jumu'ah" (Friday, the gathering) because people gather on it for the prayer. It was also said: the first person to name it "Jum'ah" was Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy, and the Arabs used to call it "al-'Aruba." It was also said that before the Hijrah the Ansar said to the Jews, "For you there is a day on which you gather every seven days, and for the Christians likewise. Come, let us make for ourselves a day on which we gather, remember God, and pray." They said: "Saturday is for the Jews and Sunday is for the Christians, so make it the day of 'Aruba." So they gathered at Sa'd ibn Zurarah, who led them in two rak'ahs and reminded them, and they named it the Day of Friday because they gathered on it. Then God revealed the verse of Friday prayer, and it was the first Friday prayer in Islam. As for the first Friday prayer that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) held: when he arrived as an emigrant, he stopped at Quba' with the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf and remained there on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and he founded their mosque. Then he set out on Friday intending Madinah, and the time of the Friday prayer overtook him among the Banu Salim ibn 'Awf, in the bottom of a valley belonging to them, so he delivered the khutbah and led the Friday prayer.

﴿So hasten to the remembrance of God⁠﴾ That is: walk and head toward the khutbah and the prayer.

﴿and leave off trade⁠﴾ and abandon dealing.

﴿That⁠﴾ i.e., the hastening to the remembrance of God and the abandoning of trade.

﴿is better for you⁠﴾ than engaging in it, for the benefit of the Hereafter is greater and more lasting.

﴿if you only knew⁠﴾ i.e., the true good and evil, or if you are people of knowledge.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 62, verse 10:

﴿Then when the prayer has been concluded﴾ (p-250)

That is: when it has been performed and finished. ﴿Then disperse throughout the land﴾, to establish your interests.

﴿And seek of Allah's bounty﴾, that is, profit. The command here is one of permission after a prohibition. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they were not commanded to seek anything of this world; rather, it means visiting the sick, attending funerals, and visiting a brother for the sake of Allah. It is related from al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab that it means seeking knowledge ('ilm). It has also been said that it means voluntary prayer (salat al-tatawwu').

﴿And remember Allah much﴾, that is, remember Him abundantly, or for a long time, and do not restrict the remembrance of Him, exalted is He, to the prayer.

﴿That you may be successful﴾, so that you may win the good of both abodes.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 62, verse 11:

﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush off to it﴾ It is narrated that the people of Madinah were afflicted by hunger and severe high prices, so Dihyah ibn Khalifah arrived with a trade caravan of olive oil from Syria while the Prophet ﷺ was delivering the Friday sermon (khutbah). The people rose and went to him, fearing they would be beaten to it, so that only eight remained with the Prophet ﷺ. It is also said: eleven. It is said: twelve. It is said: forty. The Prophet ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, had they all gone out, Allah would have kindled the valley over them with fire." And they used to, when the caravan approached, receive it with drums and clapping. This is what is meant by "diversion" (lahw). The singling out of trade in the return of the pronoun is because it was the intended object, or because rushing off to trade, though needed and beneficial, is blameworthy when it is so, so what do you think of rushing off to diversion, which is blameworthy in itself? It is also said that its estimated sense is: "when they see a trade, they rush off to it, or a diversion, they rush off to it," and the second is omitted because the first indicates it. It has also been read as "ilayhima" (to both of them).

﴿And they left you standing﴾ That is, upon the pulpit (minbar).

﴿Say: what is with Allah﴾ of reward.

﴿is better than diversion and than trade﴾ for that is a certain benefit, lasting and eternal, unlike the benefit in those two, which is merely imagined.

﴿And Allah is the best of providers﴾ so to Him strive, and from Him seek provision.

From the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever recites Surah al-Jumu'ah will be given the reward of ten good deeds for each person who attended Friday prayer and each person who did not attend it in the cities of the Muslims."
